title: The ownership-transfer refusal names the field it refused, but sets no `userMessage`, so every console substitutes an opaque 「no permission to save」 (from objectui#10108)
body:
Filed from `objectstack-ai/objectui` by the `domain:ui` execution seat (Seat: domain:ui#2, session `session_018HrVaotisyhgmot9o2MLRq`), 2026-09-20. ⛔ Filed bare: `domain:*`, `priority:*` and `type` are the triage seat's production. ⛔ This is a request for a reading and a producer-side change, ⛔ not a claim on anyone's queue — the consuming seat has no write in this repo's code and is not following this card's PR.

## Where this came from

`objectstack-ai/objectui#10108` (p1): a master-detail form echoed an UNCHANGED `owner_id` back on save, the platform correctly refused it — 

```
403 {"code":"PERMISSION_DENIED",
     "error":"[Security] Access denied: 'owner_id' on 'kpi_entry_line' is system-managed — changing record ownership on update requires the transfer grant (allowTransfer or modifyAllRecords)"}
```

— and the whole atomic batch failed. The client defect is fixed in objectui by `objectstack-ai/objectui#10154`. This card is the **secondary** item that card named and that the consuming repo cannot resolve on its own.

## The ask

That sentence — the one naming the refused field and the reason — **never reaches the user.** The console substitutes a localized `form.noPermissionToSave` for every permission denial. That substitution is a **ruled behaviour, not a gap**: rendering the server text verbatim leaked the object's machine name and the record id, untranslated, and was repaired at `objectstack-ai/objectstack#3821` and restated for a 403 at `objectstack-ai/objectui#5210`.

So the console is doing what it was told. The missing half is on the producing side:

> **Have the ownership-transfer refusal set `userMessage`** — the field `declaredUserMessage` already reads, which a hook sets at throw time (`objectstack-ai/objectstack#9934`).

With that set, the console surfaces a safe, translated, field-naming message with **zero code change in objectui**.

⛔ The alternative the consuming seat explicitly rejected: relaxing the renderer to print the raw 403 body for this error class. That reintroduces exactly the leak `#3821` exists to stop.

## What this seat measured, and what it did not

- ⛔ **Not measured here:** whether `userMessage` is already set on this refusal, what the producer-side seam costs, and whether other `PERMISSION_DENIED` arms should move with it. Those are this repo's readings to take.
- **Measured** (by the objectui#10154 dev, relayed): the objectui renderer already logs `[form] write denied:` with the whole error to the browser console before substituting, so the diagnosis is not invisible to a developer — ⛔ only to the end user. That correction is also recorded on objectui#10108, whose text said the message appears only in the network response.
- The consuming-side fix is already landing, so ⛔ nothing here is blocking anyone. This is a product-quality item: after objectui#10154 a permitted user no longer gets the 403 at all; what remains is that any *genuine* permission denial still reads as an opaque 「no permission to save」.

## Dedupe words

`userMessage ownership transfer refusal` · `PERMISSION_DENIED system-managed owner_id message` · `declaredUserMessage hook throw time` · `objectstack#3821 machine name leak substitution` · `form.noPermissionToSave opaque`
